demand_drivers.title: Mdna (RHP)
demand_drivers.body:
- Indian ceramic tile demand is supported by urbanization, growth in residential and commercial construction, increasing renovation and replacement activity, rising disposable incomes and changing consumer preferences toward aesthetically appealing and technologically advanced surfaces
- Domestic consumption is the principal growth engine for the Indian tile industry, with demand supported by residential construction, real estate activity, housing programs, and renovation/replacement expenditure
- Changing consumer preferences are creating opportunities for premium and value-added products such as glazed vitrified tiles, polished vitrified tiles, large-format tiles, designer tiles and digitally printed products
- Growth in commercial and institutional construction (hotels, offices, retail, hospitals, educational institutions, airports) provides demand opportunities beyond residential
- India's established manufacturing base and competitive production capabilities provide opportunities to expand exports into new geographies, aided by Free Trade Agreements

risks.title: Risks (RHP)
risks.body:
- The ceramic tile industry is highly competitive with organized manufacturers alongside a large regional manufacturing base; excess supply and aggressive pricing can adversely affect selling prices, dealer margins and profitability.
- Ceramic tile manufacturing is energy-intensive and highly dependent on fuel availability and prices; disruptions in LNG and propane supplies have shown the industry's vulnerability to geopolitical and energy-supply disruptions.
- Demand for tiles is closely linked to residential construction and real estate completion cycles; any slowdown in housing sales, project launches, construction activity or consumer spending could affect industry demand.
- International operations are exposed to geopolitical tensions, trade restrictions, tariffs, anti-dumping measures, sanctions, freight disruptions and changes in import regulations, which can adversely affect export volumes, realisations and profitability.
- Domestic and international operations are exposed to supply chain and logistics disruptions, foreign exchange fluctuations, and changes in international trade policies, tariffs and regulatory requirements in export markets.
- Volatility in the prices and availability of key raw materials, fuel and energy costs may impact manufacturing costs and operating margins.
- The continuous evolution of product designs, formats, finishes and manufacturing technologies requires ongoing focus on product innovation and operational efficiency to remain competitive.
